biography: Clint Field, a name synonymous with raw speed and audacious flair in the American motorsports scene, hails from the dusty plains of Oklahoma. His introduction to racing wasn't through a silver spoon; instead, it was forged in the gritty world of dirt track racing, where he honed his reflexes and learned to wrestle a car on the edge of control. Legend has it that Clint, barely a teenager, once bartered his prized collection of baseball cards for a beat-up go-kart, a decision that set the trajectory of his life. His defining moment arrived at the 2005 American Le Mans Series race at Road Atlanta. Despite facing mechanical issues and a grid penalty, Clint powered his Lola B05/40 Turbo through the field, showcasing an unparalleled level of aggression and car control. Now at his peak, Clint continues to push boundaries, leaving fans and rivals alike in breathless anticipation of his next move. He is currently focused on securing a championship title.
drivingStyle: Clint's driving style is a captivating blend of controlled aggression and instinctive brilliance. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract the maximum performance from his Lola B05/40 Turbo, often pushing the limits of grip and defying conventional racing lines. His corner entry speeds are notoriously high, and he exhibits a remarkable capacity to adapt to changing track conditions. While some might criticize his aggressive overtaking maneuvers, Clint's calculated risk-taking is often the key to his success. He is known for his ability to manage tires effectively, preserving them for crucial late-race charges.

careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2010 with a daring last-lap overtake, snatching victory from the jaws of defeat and etching his name in motorsport history.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2007 Petit Le Mans with only two laps remaining, costing his team the championship and leaving him devastated.
